title: SAG-Mem-1.0 Technical Report
abstract: arXiv:2611.33124v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long-term conversational memory requires retrieving complementary facts scattered across dialogue sessions, including intermediate evidence with limited similarity to the original question. Existing approaches often rely on derived memory representations or persistent relational structures, introducing construction costs and potentially losing source details. We present SAG-Mem, a conversational memory framework that preserves complete dialogue messages in non-overlapping chunks and discovers complementary evidence through query-time lexical expansion. Memory construction requires no model inference, using a lexical index without LLM-based extraction, summarization, or semantic relation construction. At query time, BM25 retrieves initial candidates, an evidence evaluator identifies useful chunks, and lexical cues from selected evidence guide an additional retrieval round. translated_abstract: 长期对话记忆需要检索散落在各个对话会话中的互补事实，包括与原始问题相似度有限的中间证据。现有方法通常依赖派生的记忆表示或持久化的关系结构，这会引入构建成本，并可能丢失源对话的细节。我们提出了 SAG-Mem，这是一个对话记忆框架，它将完整的对话消息保存在互不重叠的分块中，并通过查询时的词汇扩展来发现互补证据。记忆构建过程无需任何模型推理，仅使用词汇索引，而不需要基于大语言模型（LLM）的信息抽取、摘要生成或语义关系构建。在查询阶段，BM25 首先检索初始候选结果，随后证据评估器识别出有用的分块，并利用所选证据中的词汇线索引导额外一轮检索。检索到的对话内容还会进一步标注日历解释信息（原文在此处截断）。
tldr: SAG-Mem 提出了一种构建记忆时无需模型推理的对话记忆框架，通过保留完整对话分块，并在查询时利用 BM25 检索、证据评估与词汇扩展进行多轮检索，有效发现与问题相似度低但具互补性的证据。
en_tdlr: SAG-Mem is a conversational memory framework that requires no model inference during memory construction, preserving complete dialogue chunks and leveraging BM25 retrieval, evidence evaluation, and query-time lexical expansion in a multi-round process to uncover complementary evidence with limited similarity to the original question.
